**Note 199-E1 (2026-10-14 00:05 EDT; descriptive, POST-HOC, final models only; files in theory/seedstab199/emp/; CPU fp32, gate replay error ≤ 2.9e-7). Where the converged and failed classes differ in the memory.**
* **The delta write strength β, by pass (the main separator):**
  - Converged models lower β pass by pass, e.g. rms s1 / s2 0.95 → 0.44 / 0.40 over passes 1 → 8, and switch to a near-hold after the last reduction. Retention rises to 0.81–0.86 by pass 8, with a jump at the completion pass t = n + 1.
  - Failed models keep β at about 0.85–0.9 every pass (s3 0.80 → 0.89, den 0.94 → 0.86, hold 0.92 → 0.83; s188 partly, 1.02 → 0.73), and show no completion jump.
  - Every pass sees the identical input, so a pass-dependent gate can only come from the memory read. **The converged models' gates track progress; the failed models' are nearly pass-invariant.**
* **Contraction:**
  - Failed models are more contractive on average (mean log singular value −0.73 vs −0.57; retention 0.64 vs 0.73), but with no margin (s188 ≈ the converged ones), and with no gap at passes 1–2.
  - The isotropic decay α does not separate the classes.
* **Channel ablation (late passes 5–8, aux exact):**
  - Ablating the delta read kills every model (≤ 0.06).
  - Ablating the **additive think-read kills the failed models' late passes** (≤ 0.08), against 0.22–0.88 in converged models. rms s1 / s2 compute almost entirely in the delta heads.
  - So the failed models route step-to-step computation through the additive integrator. Its RMS-normalised read dilutes algebraically with each pass (docs/THEORY_SEEDSTAB Part I Lemma 1.3), which fits their per-step accuracy falling with pass index.
* **Revised account (CONJECTURE; it replaces the "contractive delta channel" wording of §199's opening as the mechanism; the order parameter stands):**
  - The working solution is a **progress-gated delta memory**: strong overwrite while computing, hold after completion. The failed solution offloads the computation to the additive integrator, under a pass-invariant overwrite.
  - The donor-start test separates the two because a pass-invariant overwrite forgets the start.
  - This also bears on overthinking: the converged models' post-completion hold (β ↓) is a learned version of Thm 3's post-completion contraction. The remaining drift after completion sits in the additive integrator and in α.
  - §199-A's CSR acts on the read displacement of both channels, so it is unaffected. Its per-head-type λ logs (csr_lam_pre_med_add / _del) will show which channel it moves.

**Clarification 200-2 (2026-10-14 00:09 EDT; before §200's gates are final and before any run; Experiments' data layer, boxes/gsm8k_data.py). Two numbers corrected. The rules are unchanged.**

This is so that constants and earlier results are never substituted.

  - Equations are recomputed in order. A draw is rejected on an evaluation error, a sign flip, or an inexactly rendered number.
  - Acceptance is 91.5%. A full check of 27,684 accepted draws: every equation evaluates exactly, and the answer equals the last result.
* **The effect:** about 55% of train items get new numbers per draw, against the draft's ~71% of numerals.
  - The R_x **dose** in B / D is lower; its definition is unchanged.
  - Theorem X's bound holds per resampled item regardless of the dose. P1 / P2 / P8 read as registered; a lower dose makes P2's RS-NEUTRAL more likely, not less.

**Note 199-A4 (2026-10-14 00:25 EDT; before any §199 cell lands; descriptive caveat from the overthinking derivation, docs/THEORY_OVERTHINK_2026-10-14.md). The limits of CSR's ceiling, for reading P-A4.**
* λ_post = log 0.5 bounds post-completion read drift to at most one last code distance (Thm A1(ii)). Certifying correct decoding needs a ceiling ≤ log(1/3), so P-A4's STABLE is not guaranteed by the target even where it is met.
* Under K = 8, items with n = 8 get **no** ceiling term, yet they carry most of the K′16 loss in the controls.
* So P-A4 (descriptive) is read per n, with n = 8 marked "untargeted".

## 201. OVERTHINK-EXIT: which memory channel drives overthinking, and can a learned halt stop it? (the user's requests via Audit, 2026-10-13 ~23:55 "also try to fix over thinking decreases acc" and 2026-10-14 ~00:0x "teach models when to transision in and out of latent thinking"; $0 eval-only on existing models; pre-registered 2026-10-14 00:27 EDT, before any §201 code or output)

**Derivation:** docs/THEORY_OVERTHINK_2026-10-14.md (9848d193; Opus subagent, reviewed by Theory). Tags as there, and the data in it are POST-HOC.
* **Part I:**
  - the additive heads have no post-completion fixed point (PROVED): the RMS read turns at about 1/t per pass toward the write direction;
  - the delta heads' fixed point under frozen inputs (PROVED) is worn down through the gate by the additive drift;
  - passes past K get zero gradient.
* **Part II:**
  - halting as quickest change detection (one-step Shiryaev threshold);
  - answer settling is uninformative before completion, which is why §173 read PREMATURE;
  - freezing all writes ≡ halting (PROVED).
* Nothing here is stacked on §199 / §200.

**Common:**
* eval-only on the final model.pt; an idle local card with no co-tenants; fp32; the card recorded;
* 1,000 test items per n (test_set, as halt173), n 2..12 and 16;
* 2,000 training-distribution items (n 2..8; train_items rng 19900) for every threshold or head fit;
* passes up to T_max = 32;
* **pooled n 3..8 = the mean of the per-n accuracies.**

**T1, FREEZE 2×2** (models: s185_rms s1 / s2, s190_rmsnopass_s1, s187_nopass s1 / s2, s184_reweight s1 / s2; negative control s182_window_s2; ProsQA s191_stepaux_relabel_s1 descriptive).
* **Arms**, with the oracle freeze point f = n + 1:
  - CLEAN;
  - FA: S_add reset to S_add,f after every write past f;
  - FD: S_delta reset to S_delta,f;
  - FB: both frozen.
* **Gates:**
  - FB's answers equal CLEAN's answer at f bitwise, at every K′ ≥ f;
  - CLEAN reproduces eval_s173_halt acc_by_t within 0.005.
* **Readout at K′ 24, pooled n 3..8:**
  - D = acc_FB − acc_CLEAN.
  - If D < 0.03, the model reads NOTHING-TO-RECOVER, a no-harm control: |acc_FA − acc_CLEAN| and |acc_FD − acc_CLEAN| ≤ 0.01.
  - Otherwise R_FA = (acc_FA − acc_CLEAN)/D and R_FD likewise, read as:
    - **ADD-COUPLED:** R_FA ≥ 0.7 and R_FD ≥ 0.5;
    - **ADD-DIRECT:** R_FA ≥ 0.7 and R_FD < 0.5;
    - **DELTA-INTRINSIC:** R_FD ≥ 0.7 and R_FA ≤ 0.3;
    - **JOINT:** both ≤ 0.3;
    - otherwise **mixed**.
  - K′ 16 / 32 and n 9–10 are beside, descriptive.
* **Predictions:**
  - **T1-a:** rms s1 / s2 and §190 s1 read ADD-COUPLED;
  - **T1-b:** §184 s1 / s2 read ADD-DIRECT or ADD-COUPLED, with R_FD < R_FA.
* **Falsifier:** in ≥ 2 of {rms s1, rms s2, §190 s1}, R_FA ≤ 0.3, i.e. the additive-integrator account of converged-model overthinking is false.

**T2, HALT** (the same nested models; features from T1's CLEAN dump).
* **PRIMARY = SHIRYAEV-HEAD:**
  - a logistic π̂_t for label 1[t ≥ n], fit on training items only;
  - features: answer max-prob, entropy and top-2 margin; answer-change flags at t−1 and t−2; the AUX-DONE bit and probability; β̄_t and retention ρ_t per head and their one-pass differences; additive and delta read relative increments. **No t, and no additive norm.**
  - **Stop** at the first t with π̂_t ≥ A = p̂·C_FA/(p̂·C_FA + c_d). p̂, C_FA and c_d are estimated on training items as in docs/THEORY_OVERTHINK Part V.
  - **Censoring:** a rule that never fires stops at T_max with the answer at T_max. It counts in every accuracy; the event-only mean halt and the censored share are reported beside.
* **Comparators:** the best fixed K′ chosen on TRAINING items, and K′ = n + 2 per n.
* **Readings per model:**
  - **NO-OVERTHINK:** pooled n 3..8 ≥ acc(best fixed K′) − 0.01;
  - **SIZE-FREE:** at n 9 and 10, acc ≥ acc(K′ n+2) − 0.03, with the event-only mean halt in [n−1, n+3] and censored ≤ 0.10;
  - **PREMATURE:** ≥ 0.05 below K′ n+2 at any n ∈ 3..10.
* **Predictions:**
  - **T2-a:** NO-OVERTHINK on all 7 nested models;
  - **T2-b:** SIZE-FREE at n 9 on rms s1 and s2, and at n 10 on s2;
  - **T2-c:** §184 s1 / s2 PREMATURE, or censored share > 0.10 at n 10.
* **Falsifier of the β cue (T2-b):** on both RMS seeds, ≥ 50% of n = 10 halts fall at t ∈ {8, 9} **and** the rule's n = 10 accuracy is ≥ 0.05 below K′12.
* **Descriptive rules** (AUX-DONE, MIN-BETA, RET-JUMP, CONF, TRM-HEAD, answer2 / MOVED2) and the per-n AUROC are reported beside.
* **Halting is not expected to raise the peak.** A tuned fixed K′ is within 0.03 of the per-n oracle (POST-HOC). The gains are robustness past K and compute.

**Not registered here:**
* T3 (reading CSR's post-completion behaviour when §199's cells land);
* T4 (SNAP-CHAIN text checkpoints, the ENTRY / EXIT half);
* T5 (a training cell, ≤ $10).
Each registers separately, after T1 / T2.

**Outputs and scorer:** `<run>/eval_s201_freeze.json` and `<run>/eval_s201_halt.json` (schemas in theory/score_s201.py's docstring), read by theory/score_s201.py, which is fixture-checked before any output.

**Note 199-A5 (2026-10-14 10:57 EDT; BEFORE s1's landing readout; Theory has seen only Audit's relay of s1's live loss bins (about 1.41 at 44.5k, never entered, against the paired control's 19k entry). Descriptive diagnostic, pre-stated.) A candidate mechanism for CSR harm, gradient crowding, and the check that reads it.**
* **Derivation flaw (Theory's own, DERIVED):** λ_t is scale-free in **value**, but not in **gradient**.
  - With R = fade·W_o·o, ∂log‖R_{t+1} − R_t‖/∂W_o = (ΔR Δoᵀ)/‖ΔR‖², which has magnitude ∝ 1/‖W_o‖ (for fixed Δo).
  - CSR switches on at step 500, when W_o has just faded in from 0 and is small, so its gradient on the memory branch is ∝ 1/‖W_o‖ and can be very large.
  - Under the global-norm clip (binding on about all steps), a large CSR gradient shrinks the CE / aux share of every update. That is **gradient crowding**, which could prevent entry regardless of the contraction account.
  - 199-A's Thm A2 (scalar model) did not model this. It is a dose / schedule property of the registered w = 0.1 at start step 500, not of the target's sign structure.
* **Diagnostic, $0, on the kept CSR checkpoints at 4k / 8k / 12k / 16k (Experiments):** on 4 batches of 64 training items, the gradient norms G_csr = ‖∇(0.1·CSR)‖ and G_task = ‖∇(CE + aux)‖. Report the ratio, overall and on the memory-branch parameters, plus ‖W_o‖.
  - **GRADIENT-CROWDING:** G_csr / G_task ≥ 1 on the memory branch at 4k or 8k.
  - Otherwise **NOT-CROWDED**. CSR's harm then has another cause, and the P-A5 reading carries the weight.
* **The registered label is untouched.** The per-seed label (INSUFFICIENT-DOSE / FALSIFIER / FLOOR-GAMED / ENTERED) is read exactly as registered. This diagnostic is reported beside it.
  - If it reads CROWDING, any re-test of CSR (a new registration) would need a gradient-normalised or warm-started dose, with its own derivation.

**Note 199-A5a (2026-10-14 10:57 EDT; before s1's landing readout).** How 199-A5's diagnostic qualifies the P-A5 label.
* P-A5's falsifier logic ("non-contractive by the order parameter, yet not entered, so contraction is not the barrier") assumes the task gradient was still training the model.
* If the diagnostic reads **GRADIENT-CROWDING** (G_csr / G_task ≥ 1 on the memory branch at 4k or 8k), a FALSIFIER label is reported as **"FALSIFIER, confounded by gradient crowding"**: non-entry has an alternative cause (a starved task gradient).
  - The contraction account is then neither confirmed nor cleanly falsified by this seed.
  - The **method** reading is unaffected: CSR as registered (w 0.1, start 500) failed on the paired seed.
* If the diagnostic reads NOT-CROWDED, a FALSIFIER label stands unqualified.
* FLOOR-GAMED / INSUFFICIENT-DOSE readings carry the diagnostic beside them.

**Note 199-A5b (2026-10-14 10:57 EDT; disclosure, Audit).** 199-A5 and 199-A5a were both written **before s1's landing readout but after** Audit's 10:5x relay of s1's interim live log (not entered at 44.5k; bins about 1.41). The crowding qualifier is pre-landing, post-interim-log. It changes no verdict: the method reading is untouched either way.

**Note 201-7 (2026-10-14 11:17 EDT; before any output; $0 eval-only; the ENTRY / EXIT half of the user's "teach models when to transition in and out of latent thinking"). T4, SNAP-CHAIN: when does writing a text checkpoint beat more latent passes?**
* **Derivation:** docs/THEORY_OVERTHINK_2026-10-14.md Part III, Prop. 8 (PROVED, given two horizons).
  - A single checkpoint at pass k needs k ≤ H_L (the latent is reliable) and n − k ≤ H_W (the remainder is decodable as a step string). So it reaches n ≤ H_L + H_W ≈ 14–15.
  - More checkpoints do not extend that.
  - The write-late rule is k* = H_L. A checkpoint also resets the integrator, so no segment enters the untrained post-K region.
* **Models:** §190 s1, rms s1 / s2, §184 s2. **Items:** n ∈ {9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16}, 1,000 each (test_set as halt173). fp32, an idle local card.
* **Write step W:**
  - greedily decode the step text e_{t+1} with the model's own aux decoder (its own prompt);
  - if it parses as a valid expression of the grammar, restart with think input [EOT, e_{t+1}, " ."] and S = 0, and the answer decoder sees e_{t+1} as the expression;
  - otherwise continue latent.
* **Policies:**
  - **LATENT-BEST:** the best fixed K′ chosen on training items (§201 T2);
  - **LATENT-HALT:** §201 T2's primary halt;
  - **TIMEOUT7 (PRIMARY):** latent until the T2 halt fires; if it has not fired by pass 7, W at 7. Each later segment follows the same rule, with ≤ 3 checkpoints, and the final segment halts by T2's rule (cap 32 total);
  - **FIX2 / FIX4 / FIX7:** W at that pass (≤ 3 checkpoints);
  - **LEN-IN-RANGE:** W at the first pass whose decoded string has ≤ 7 operators.
* **Measured per n:**
  - accuracy;
  - mean total passes, including after checkpoints;
  - mean decoded tokens;
  - q_W, the greedy whole-string aux exact match at the write pass;
  - the parse-valid share;
  - per-segment K′ = 0 accuracy (T4-d).
* **Readings (per model, PRIMARY TIMEOUT7; n 11–12 pooled = the mean of the n 11 and n 12 accuracies):**
  - LAT = max(LATENT-BEST, LATENT-HALT) at n 11–12;
  - **SNAP-HELPS:** TIMEOUT7 ≥ LAT + 0.15, with mean total passes ≤ best fixed K′ + 4;
  - **SNAP-NEUTRAL:** within ±0.05;
  - **SNAP-HURTS:** ≤ LAT − 0.05;
  - otherwise **mixed**.
* **Predictions:**
  - **T4-a:** SNAP-HELPS on §190 s1, conditional on its q_W at pass 7 ≥ 0.6 (n 11–12 mean).
  - **T4-b:** at n 11–12, FIX7 ≥ FIX4 ≥ FIX2. **Falsifier:** FIX4 > FIX7 + 0.05.
  - **T4-c (reach boundary):** n 14 is helped (TIMEOUT7 ≥ LAT_14 + 0.15) and n 16 is not. **Falsifier:** n 16 helped by ≥ 0.15.
  - **T4-d:** per-segment K′ = 0 accuracy at chance (descriptive).
* **Output:** `<run>/eval_s201_snap.json` = {"policies": {NAME: {"acc_by_n", "mean_passes_by_n", "mean_tokens_by_n"}}, "qW_kw7_by_n", "parse_valid_by_n", "segment_k0_by_n", "best_fixed_k_train"}.
  - Reader: theory/score_s201_t4.py, fixture-checked before any output.

## 202. WARM-START-FROM-COT: does a CoT-trained trunk make §200's latent arm competitive at equal exposure? (the user's pre-approval relayed by Audit, 2026-10-14 ~12:0x, "ima preapprove wtv yall cooking up", ≤ $4; triggered by §200 reading BELOW; pre-registered 2026-10-14 16:41 EDT, before any §202 code or run)

**Derivation and probes:** docs/THEORY_WARMCOT_DRAFT_2026-10-14.md (f368b9ca; Opus subagent, reviewed by Theory). Literature's check is d29ff05b. Tags as there; the probe data are POST-HOC.
* **Decomposition:** the latent step task splits into (i) arithmetic, (ii) the plan (the next expression from the word problem), and (iii) routing through the memory.
  - **Lemma R (PROVED, code):** the aux decoder's read query is item-independent where it emits the first operand.
  - **Lemma O (PROVED, code):** the think pass gets zero aux gradient until γ > 0.
  - So the plan must be written by the think pass, and its learning signal is a product, plan-present × route-present (Lemma S: products of small factors escape slowly).
  - A CoT-trained trunk supplies (ii) at step 0, which acts as a **tilt** in docs/THEORY_SEEDSTAB Part II's selection law (DERIVED|A1–A4).
* **Precondition P-W0 (probe, POST-HOC): met for the operator, NOT for the operand.**
  - C's think-pass features carry e_1's operator: +0.06 valid / +0.09–0.11 held-out over raw GPT-2.
  - They do not carry the first-operand slot (C − raw ≤ +0.03 at every position).
  - At C's own emission position ("<<"), C's LM head selects the operand at 0.657 valid. That is a partial probe, C only.
  - So the warm start supplies **half** the plan. Operand selection must still be learned as written content (CONJECTURE: this limits W).
* **§200's reality:** A formed a weak, mostly one-pass loop (K′10 − K′0 0.064; K′1 0.125 ≈ K′10 0.147), so §200's failure is accuracy, not loop formation. **The primary question is therefore the accuracy lift**, not W-INIT's formation test.
* **Field convention (Literature 95a7fb15 / d29ff05b):**
  - every published GPT-2 GSM8K-Aug latent number is CoT-supervised;
  - Coconut's stage 0: 31.1 vs 22.3 without it;
  - CODI: a joint CoT CE **without** its L1 coupling gives 24.5 vs 43.7 (no-CoT 19.1), so joint training needs a coupling.
  - **This matches the field's initialisation; it is not a new method.**
  - The new element is a removal test pre-registered with the training run, paired with an equal-exposure text control. Dilgren & Wiegreffe 2604.04902 ran post-hoc removal on Coconut / CODI and is related work.

**Cells** (RTX 3090, seed 1, bs 64, lr 1e-4, warm-up 100 + cosine over 12k; run dirs in boxes/runs_fsq/; the final checkpoint for every reading, the Aug-valid-selected one beside it; **the test is never used for selection**):

## 203. SVR (shallow value readout): a seed-stability successor to CSR (the user's novel-method request; USER APPROVED 2026-10-14 ~19:0x, "approve 12 and clean", relayed verbatim by Audit, ≤ $10.10; pre-registered 2026-10-14 19:13 EDT, before any §203 code or run)

**Registered text:**
* docs/THEORY_SEEDSTAB2_DRAFT_2026-10-14.md **at cee1d8d9** (rev 3 plus the gate-results appendix) is the registered text for every definition used below: §4.1 SVR, §4.3 the use tests, §5 Goodhart, §6 gradient flow, §7 cells / fields / predictions / labels / gates / engineering.
* That file is now frozen. Changes go here as dated amendments.
* Derivation by Opus subagent; Theory reviewed it twice.
  - Rev 1's per-head-normalised readout could compute mod-11 ops (theory/seedstab2/perhead_norm.json), so the readout map is now linear.
  - Audit's two points (presence ≠ use; the separator's direction) are in rev 3.
* Tags as there. All data are POST-HOC.

**Method.**
* A training-only cosine readout (11-way, τ = 10, **no bias**) on the delta-head reads of S_t (G-pre PASSED, so delta heads only).
* Inputs: the reads at the answer decoder's own " =" query (stop-gradient), each head scaled by a stop-gradient EMA constant. The argmax is a linear functional of S_t.
* Target: v_t, the value of reduction t, for t ≤ n.
* Loss weight: w·γ(step), with w = 1. The weight is exactly 0 while the loop is open, so the cells are bitwise identical to their controls to step 2000.
* No pass token, no item text, dropped at test (model.pt excludes svr.*). C1 is kept.

**Why (claims as tagged in the draft).**
* **G1 (PROVED):** targets read through the pass-aware full-trunk aux decoder are met by the contractive class, because the reader reduces.
* **G2 (PROVED):** displacement floors, bands and ceilings are met without content. This is CSR's FLOOR-GAMED.
* **Lemma L (PROVED, rev 2 map):** the readout cannot reduce superposed operand codes.
* **S1 / S2 (PROVED):** a stalled state pays a floor that is not diluted by target length.
* **Lemma 4 correction (PROVED):** the NOPASS penalty is about 2 ln 2/(L+1) per pass pair.
* **CERT (DERIVED under the empirical one-pass ceiling A1′, with guards g1 / g2).**
* **The tilt (DERIVED / CONJECTURE).** SVR is a tilt, not a removal (Prop R).

**Cells (RTX 3090; 48k; s185 RMS recipe exactly + `--svr 1.0,10` + `--keep_ckpt_steps 4000,8000,12000,16000`).**
* `s203_svr_s1` / `s2` / `s3`, each paired with s185_rms_s{seed}:
  - log records 100–2000 bitwise equal on loss, answer_ce and aux_ce;
  - the control's driver (s1 / s2 570.172.08, s3 595.84);
  - micro 1. Otherwise UNPAIRED.
* **C8k** `s203_c8k_s1` / `s2` / `s3`: each control's args run to 8k on its driver, keeping ckpt_model_8000.pt. PAIRED-C8k if records 100–8000 are bitwise equal to the s185 log.
* C16k is not run (optional in the draft, outside this approval).

**Launch condition (pre-launch, $0; the user's scope).**
* **G-pre: PASSED** (cee1d8d9). DELTA separates the 16 models: t2 0.633 > 0.345, t3 0.452 > 0.239.
* **G-use** (draft §7 rule, fixed at 17c06299 before any G-use output), on the 9 converged final models:
  - **≥ 7 / 9 USED → launch**;
  - **≤ 4 / 9 → do not launch**;
  - **5–6 / 9 → back to the user.** This tightens the draft's "launch with the fact reported", per the user's scope via Audit.
* The ALL-heads diagnostic (cee1d8d9, POST-HOC, added after model 1's delta-only ABL-NULL) is reported beside it. If the registered count is ≤ 6 / 9 while ALL reads USED, both go to the user.
* Then: the gates G0–G6, G-abl and G-swap (draft §7), Audit's diff review, the pairing check, and a running cost guard at $10.10.

**Readings and predictions (definitions as in the draft §7; theory/score_s203.py, fixture-checked before launch):**
* **Per-seed labels (final model):** ENTERED-AND-USED / MET-NOT-USED / MET-NOT-ENTERED / ENTERED-UNMET / INSUFFICIENT-DOSE / USE-UNCLEAR / PRECOMPUTE-GAMED / ONE-PASS-COMPUTE.
  - MET = DELIVERED (svr_acc_t2p ≥ 0.35 over 47001–48000) or CERT (svr_acc_h5p ≥ 0.30 there, with g1 K′=1 at n 3–8 ≤ 0.20 and g2 the pass-1 deep probe ≤ 0.21).
  - USED = the §4.3 (a) ablation differential, or the (b) swap follows.
* **Arm:**
  - SUPPORTED = 3 / 3 ENTERED-AND-USED, with CERT and P-V4, and no HARMFUL;
  - FAILED = any HARMFUL, or s3 MET-NOT-ENTERED, or any MET-NOT-USED;
  - otherwise MIXED.
* **P-V0** (8k dose, paired): SVR − C8k step_recover mean over t 2–4 ≥ +0.15 in 3 / 3. A miss reads EARLY-DOSE-MISSED.
* **C8k-expect / direction:** EARLY-MARKER vs NO-EARLY vs AMBIGUOUS. The 2×2 is read with the s3 SVR outcome, under the draft's wording limit: no 8k presence ≠ non-causal.
* **P-V2:** entry(0.5) ≤ 24k and final bin < 0.1. **P-V3 / HARMFUL:** s1 or s2 never enters (their controls entered at 19k).
* **P-V4:** acc_from_zero ≥ 0.95 and (delta_cos ≤ 0.65 or acc_from_donor ≥ 0.9). **P-V5** and OP-8k are descriptive.
* **Account falsifier:** MET-NOT-ENTERED with USED, path-dependent (final delta_cos ≤ 0.65), and NOT-CROWDED (G_svr/G_task < 1 at 4k and 8k).
* **Claim limits:**
  - P(3 / 3 | p = 2 / 3) = 0.30, and P(s3 enters | no effect) ≈ 0.6;
  - the mechanism labels carry the reading;
  - a P(enter) claim needs a second-stage panel (the user's call).

**Cost:** about $8.5 central, $10.1 high (3 cells $6.6–8.7 + C8k $1.1–1.4). Approved ≤ $10.10, and the guard alerts at it. Realised $ replaces the projection at landing.

**Note 203-1 (2026-10-14 19:14 EDT; prior art; no rule change). Literature's novelty check, docs/LIT_SVR_NOVELTY_2026-10-14.md (ccfc0543; IDs verified on the arXiv abstract pages). It supersedes the draft §8 novelty rows where they differ.**
* **KNOWN:** per-step intermediate-value supervision through shared linear decoders, i.e. CLRS hints (2205.15659) and the Generalist learner (2209.11142, which feeds its predictions back; SVR does not). This is the closest precedent.
* **RISK evidence for presence ≠ use**, which §4.3's use tests and the MET-NOT-USED label exist to catch:
  - Rodionov & Prokhorenkova 2306.13411: hint-aligned, but no dependency on the result;
  - "Cosine Misleads" 2606.05753: supervised latents are largely bypassed, with r = −0.94 between alignment and accuracy;
  - 2606.12689: decodable patterns appear in controls too.
* **NEW (the claim line):**
  - a selectivity-constrained head (linear, bias-free, pass-free, stop-gradient query, never fed back) that is derived to be unable to compute the value (Lemma L), used as a loss;
  - on a pretrained LM's recurrent memory;
  - aimed at seed-robust basin entry.
* **Wording to avoid in any §203 result:** "first per-step value supervision", "first probe-as-loss", and anything that treats decodability as use.

**§203 result: G-use reads DO NOT LAUNCH (2026-10-14 19:24 EDT; Experiments 5b2b9994, eval_svr_guse.json on the 9 converged D7 final models, 4060 bf16; registered rule fixed at 17c06299, before any G-use output). D7's linear value separator is decodable but unused: NOT-USED 9 / 9. SVR is not run, so $0 of the ≤ $10.10 is spent.**
* **Per model** (base accuracy K′ 8, n 3–8 on 2,400 items; ablation of V_probe at every delta read; pass-2 rank-1 donor swap on 2,252 items):
  - drop(V) ≤ 0.0004 in every model.
  - Δ_rank −0.002 to +0.0003; Δ_E −0.062 to −0.002, with every CI below +0.06. So **ABL-NULL 9 / 9**.
  - F − F_null between −0.0014 and 0. The swap's own-accuracy disruption is 0. So **IGNORES 9 / 9**.
  - Base accuracy 0.90–1.00.
* **USED 0 / 9**, against the ≤ 4 / 9 line. **The registered outcome is DO NOT LAUNCH; return to Theory.**
* **Caveats, stated:**
  - **G-abl (the ablation's validity gate: probe accuracy after projection = chance ± 0.02) fails as written on s190_rmsnopass_s1 and s182_window_s1.** Both read 0.0687.
    - Under P_V the probe's class logits differ only by its bias, so it predicts one constant class (U1 as intended). Its accuracy is that class's test frequency, which here lies 0.002 outside the band.
    - The gate is not reinterpreted after output. For those two, NOT-USED rests on the swap arm alone.
    - The verdict is unchanged: 7 / 9 with both arms valid read NOT-USED.
  - **The energy-matched controls are not energy-matched.** V carries 0.6–1.1% of the read energy (E_V 11.2 of 1,012 on rms s1). Every Σ^β candidate removes about 10× more (E 122–132), which makes Δ_E negative by construction. The NULL reading rests on drop(V) ≈ 0 and Δ_rank ≈ 0, which need no energy matching.
* **Reading:**
  - The standardised linear probe (D7) separates converged from failed models through low-energy directions that the converged models' own computation does not use.
  - It is a correlate of convergence, not the mechanism.
  - This matches the presence ≠ use evidence of note 203-1 (2606.05753, 2606.12689) and the decodable-but-unused risk that rev 3 added the gate for.
  - SVR's rationale (training the property behind D7) fails before any spend.
* **Not tested:** whether a *used* value representation exists elsewhere, in other directions, non-linearly, or by magnitude.
  - That is the next question (DAS-USED, a $0 diagnostic draft in progress; Literature 2b6bfd25).
  - Only a causally used separator could justify a supervision target.
* **The ALL-heads diagnostic** (POST-HOC, descriptive; cee1d8d9) is running on all 9. On s185_rms_s1: ABL-NULL, and the swap IGNORES with edit success 0.854 and fidelity cos 0.9999. The result is appended when complete. If ALL reads USED anywhere, it goes to the user beside the registered count.
  - *(Appended 2026-10-14 20:12 EDT.)* **ALL-heads diagnostic complete: ABL-NULL + IGNORES on 9 / 9**, so nothing goes to the user beyond the registered count.
    - Ablation: drop(V) 0.0000 on 8 models and −0.0013 on one.
    - Swap: the exact additive edit on the 5 no-norm models (fidelity cos 1.0000, edit success 0.71–0.90) and the direction-only edit on the 4 RMS models (cos 0.9999, edit success 0.84–0.91). F = F_null in every model; disruption ≤ 0.002.
    - **The answer path ignores a faithfully written donor value in both head types.**

**Note 203-2 (2026-10-14 20:37 EDT; pre-stated before any output; descriptive, $0 local; step 1 of the Audit-approved DAS-USED pilot, docs/THEORY_DASUSED_DRAFT_2026-10-14.md). CONDITIONED SERIAL: does the whole-state swap contrast survive conditioning on capability?**
* **Why:**
  - s170.serial at t = 2 reads a hybrid rate of 0.53–0.96 in the 9 converged models and 0.07–0.12 in the 7 failed.
  - The failed models solve shallow items clean at K′ = K (s185_rms_s3: 0.96 / 0.84 / 0.65 at n 3 / 4 / 5). After the swap, though, they give the recipient's own answer only 0.12–0.31 of the time.
  - So "failed = non-solver" does not explain it, but the class contrast has not been conditioned on capability (Audit).
* **Protocol:** nested170's own serial test (serial_items(SPOOL, rng 17200); the 476 pairs; swap the whole state after pass t ∈ {1, 2}, then K passes) on the 16 D7 final models.
  - Re-run with **per-pair rows**: the swapped answer, plus each model's clean answers on the recipient and the donor without a swap, at K′ = K.
  - One card per model, bf16, the original eval batch size (the bf16 rule). bs, card and dtype are recorded.
* **Gate:** the unconditioned rates (hybrid / donor / recipient at t = 1, 2) reproduce eval.json s170.serial within 0.02.
* **Readings:**
  - hybrid / donor / recipient on **CLEAN pairs** (recipient and donor both answered correctly at K′ = K without a swap), at t = 2 (primary) and t = 1, overall and by recipient n, each with its count;
  - a model with fewer than 100 clean pairs at t = 2 is N/A, not "absent".
  - **CONTRAST-SURVIVES:** min over converged clean hybrid − max over failed clean hybrid ≥ 0.20 at t = 2, with ≥ 5 failed models non-N/A.
  - **CAPABILITY-EXPLAINED:** some failed model's clean hybrid ≥ the converged minimum − 0.10.
  - Otherwise **AMBIGUOUS**.
  - Descriptive: on clean pairs, also the failed models' clean-pair recipient rate, i.e. whether the swap disrupts items they otherwise solve.
* **Consequence:** CONTRAST-SURVIVES supports a whole-state interchange loss (IIT-SERIAL, being drafted) as a target that separates the basins. CAPABILITY-EXPLAINED weakens it to "converged models use their state; failed models' failure is not specific to state use".

  - It supports a whole-state interchange loss (docs/THEORY_IITSERIAL_DRAFT_2026-10-14.md) as a target aimed at the actual difference.
  - The direction is not tested: final models only, so state use may be a consequence of entry. Only the intervention tests the cause.

**Note 203-5 (2026-10-14 21:14 EDT; pre-stated before any output; descriptive, $0 eval-only; Audit's lead after 203-4). CONSUMED-MASK: do failed seeds need the re-read input at later passes because they recompute from it?**
* **Why:**
  - 203-4: failed seeds ignore a carried state and return their own answer, which fits think passes that re-converge to an input-determined state (Part I's contraction class). Converged seeds carry and use the state.
  - So hiding the input tokens whose content was already reduced at earlier passes should cost the converged class little and the failed class a lot.
  - The literature framing (input re-injection in looped models: 2609.01924, SCSE 2607.27656, OrthoInj 2610.06833; IDs pending Literature) is a conjecture for transfer. None of them tests reasoning or seed stability.
* **Manipulation (think passes only, t ≥ 2; the answer decoder's [EOT, expr, " ="] stays clean in the primary arm):**
  - Reductions follow the generator's own order (reductions(root), the aux targets' schedule).
  - At think pass t, every token in the original-expression span of each subtree reduced at passes 1..t−1 is replaced by one fixed filler token. That token is " ?", or another single GPT-2 token outside VOCAB, chosen and asserted single-token before the run. Length and positions are unchanged.
  - Passes run to the model's own K.
* **Arms:**
  - **M-CONS (primary):** consumed spans masked as above.
  - **M-UNCONS (specificity control):** the same number of tokens masked at each pass, drawn from spans NOT yet consumed by pass t−1 (the latest-reduced subtrees first; rng 20391).
  - **M-CONS-ANS (descriptive):** M-CONS plus the same masking on the answer decoder's input.
* **Items:** test items with n 3–8 (≤ 1,000 per n, rng 20381) that the model answers correctly clean at K′ = K. The readable minimum is 100 clean items per model. Reported overall and by n.
* **Readings** (retained = accuracy under the arm, on the model's own clean items):
  - **TOLERANCE-SEPARATES:** min over converged retained(M-CONS) − max over failed retained(M-CONS) ≥ 0.25, with ≥ 5 failed readable.
  - **NO-SEPARATION:** the gap is ≤ 0.10. Otherwise AMBIGUOUS.
  - **Audit's predictions:** converged drop ≤ 0.15, failed drop ≥ 0.40.
  - **Specificity (descriptive):** converged retained(M-CONS) − retained(M-UNCONS) ≥ 0.20, i.e. they need the unconsumed text but not the consumed text.
  - **Pre-stated risk:** a converged drop under M-CONS together with a large M-UNCONS drop would mean masking disrupts memory addressing (writes keyed on those positions), not recomputation. It is reported as MASK-DISRUPTS.
* **Gates:**
  - the filler token is single and outside VOCAB;
  - no masking at t = 1 gives answers bitwise equal to the clean eval at the same bs / card;
  - the consumed spans for each item are checked against e_t on 10k generator items (the span replaced by its value reproduces e_t).
  - One card (3070), bf16, the original eval bs; card / dtype / bs recorded.
* **Consequence:** only TOLERANCE-SEPARATES motivates a SOURCE-DAMPED training variant. That would be its own derivation and the user's call, presented beside IIT-SERIAL, not instead of it.

**Note 203-6 (2026-10-14 21:14 EDT; pre-stated before any output; descriptive, $0 eval-only; Literature a44a9948). INPUT-SWAP, the mirror of the SERIAL state swap: does a model follow its carried state or its re-presented input?**
* **Why:** Wang & Reid 2609.01924 (Huginn): an injection swap from recurrence k flips the output to the new input's answer in 30 / 30 configurations, i.e. "continuous recomputation from the re-injected input". They call for matched small looped models with and without that behaviour. 203-4 shows our failed seeds ignore a swapped state. This test checks the other side.
* **Manipulation:**
  - Think passes 1..k run on the recipient's input x_r.
  - Passes k + 1..K and the answer decoder run on a donor's input x_d. The donor is structure-matched: the same tree shape, with the leaves of nodes reduced at passes ≤ k differing so that their values differ.
  - The memory is carried unchanged.
  - k ∈ {1, 2}. Items are test n 3–8 (≤ 1,000 per n, rng 20401). Eligibility: height(root) ≥ 2k + 1.
* **Targets** (all exact from the trees):
  - y_d, the donor's own answer;
  - **y_mir**, the mirror hybrid: the donor's tree with the nodes reduced at passes ≤ k set to the recipient's values;
  - y_r, the recipient's answer.
  - Kept: y_mir ∉ {y_d, y_r}.
* **Readings,** on clean-ccc pairs (the model answers x_r, x_d and the mirror item correctly clean; minimum 100 per model), at k = 1 (primary) and k = 2:
  - **STATE-FOLLOW** = P(answer = y_mir);
  - **INPUT-FOLLOW** = P(answer = y_d).
* **Predicted, as the 2 × 2 with 203-4:**
  - converged: STATE-FOLLOW ≥ 0.6 and INPUT-FOLLOW ≤ 0.3, the mirror of their SERIAL hybrid ≥ 0.70;
  - failed: INPUT-FOLLOW ≥ 0.8, the mirror of their SERIAL own-answer ≥ 0.87.
  - **DISSOCIATES:** both hold for every readable model with ≥ 5 failed readable. **NO-DISSOCIATION:** the converged models' INPUT-FOLLOW is ≥ 0.6, i.e. they also recompute from the input. Otherwise AMBIGUOUS.
* **Gates:**
  - with x_d = x_r, answers are bitwise equal to the clean eval at the same bs / card;
  - the structure match and y_mir are checked on 10k generator items (the swapped values change the mirror answer);
  - one card (3070), bf16, the original eval bs, recorded.

* **203-5 (CONSUMED-MASK) is kept as registered.**

**Note 203-9: the DAS-USED pilot P2 k-ladder, rms s1 (2026-10-15 00:12 EDT; descriptive; Experiments 35bf38de; 3070, t = 2, lr 3e-3, B n_ccc 4,471; stopping rule fixed in the DAS draft at f89bc03e before any k ≥ 64 output).   - every fit early-stopped on flat validation (400–900 steps of the 2,000 / 5,000 caps);

  - By the pre-fixed rule: **"no compact used subspace ≤ 1024-d found (distributed or fit-limited)".**
  - No P2 on the other 3 pilots and no Stage B.
  - *(Reworded 00:13 per Audit, to the rule's label.)* The swap is causal at the whole-state level (203-3 / 203-4: swap-follow 0.80–0.97 in converged models). Whether a compact subspace carries it is **undecided: distributed or fit-limited** (the fitter reached only 0.46 train at k 1024). The fit-free PCA check below decides it.

    - ≥ 0.8 at some k ≤ 4096 reads **COMPACT-FIT-LIMITED** (the fitter, not the code, was the bottleneck).
    - < 0.5 at 16384 reads **DISTRIBUTED** (Csordás 2408.10920's onion / magnitude codes are the frame).
    - Otherwise INTERMEDIATE.

    - The basis needs ≥ k independent differences, so the 4,000 A pairs cap the rank at 4,000. **The pool is ≥ 20,000 fresh pairs** built like B (same donor construction and eligibility), drawn from items disjoint from B (new rng 20501), with a randomized SVD; the method is recorded.
    - k ∈ {1024, 4096, 16384}, evaluated on the B ccc pairs only.

**Note 203-9b: the fit-free PCA swap (2026-10-15 00:37 EDT; the 203-9 amendment's pre-stated check; Experiments; rms s1, t = 2, B ccc n 4,471; basis = exact PCA (20k × 20k Gram, float64) of a SEPARATE 20,000-pair pool, rng 20501, disjoint from B). COMPACT-FIT-LIMITED: the DAS ladder's null was the fitter, not the code.**
* **Results:**

  | k (top PCA directions of S_d − S_r) | ycf (IIA_ccc) | own | B difference energy captured |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1024 | 0.707 | 0.149 | 0.982 |
  | 4096 | **0.905** | 0.042 | 0.996 |
  | 16384 | 0.914 | 0.038 | 0.9994 |

  - The whole-state swap reads 0.915.
  - At k = 4096, ycf is 0.89–0.93 at every n 3–8.
* **The rule (≥ 0.8 at some k ≤ 4096) reads COMPACT-FIT-LIMITED.** DAS at k ≤ 1024 read about 0.09–0.10, while the unoptimised PCA basis it was warm-started from already scores 0.707 at k = 1024. So the QR-parameterised fit at lr 3e-3 moved away from a good initialisation within the first 100 steps and early-stopped on flat validation.
* **Scope of "compact" (stated):**
  - 4096 directions hold 99.6% of the item-to-item difference energy. So this shows that **the item-varying part of S_2 lives in about 4096 of 49,152 dimensions (8%)**, and swapping it transfers the computation.
  - It does **not** identify a v₂-SPECIFIC code. That would need a DAS fit that beats PCA at a given k, which the pilot's fitter never achieved.
* **Archive P2** (4060, k ≤ 64; 0f1b16fb): label **VOID** (G-DISRUPT: a same-value patch drops own accuracy 0.82–0.88). Descriptive: necessity resample excess 0.76; locus additive 0.83. No weight.
* **Methodology lesson:** DAS fits must log validation at step 0 (the initialisation) and keep "best including init". A warm start can be destroyed by the step size.
* **Optional, not queued:** a refit from the PCA-1024 basis at lr 1e-4 with step-0 validation, to test whether a v₂-specific subspace beats PCA. It is descriptive and does not affect IIT-SERIAL.
* *(Done 2026-10-15 01:31 EDT, 65b97269; descriptive.)* From the PCA-1024 init (B IIA_ccc 0.707, val 0.710), Adam at lr 1e-4 drops val to 0.142 within 100 steps and early-stops at 300; best = the init (kept). **Likely mechanism (descriptive, untested):** R = QR(W) with W ∈ R^{49,152 × k} has entries of about 1/√49,152 ≈ 0.0045, and Adam moves each entry by about lr per step regardless of gradient scale. So the basis is randomised within tens of steps (lr 1e-4) or a few (lr 3e-3). A fit in this parameterisation needs lr ~1e-6–1e-5 or a scale-aware optimiser.

**Note 204-1 (2026-10-14 19:16 EDT; prior art plus one pre-stated external check; no rule change). Literature's D1 novelty pass, docs/LIT_STEPFACTOR_D1_2026-10-14.md (f527a2d0).**
* **Not found in the literature.** CODI, SIM-CoT and PCCoT were read in full text, and RiM was checked.
  - SIM-CoT teacher-forces its step decoder on the step string with no leak discussion.
  - CODI names a *different* shortcut: copying the final result into the answer-token activations.
  - RiM's within-step targets are teacher-forced, so D1 applies to them unremarked.
* **Parent principle:** Bachmann & Nagarajan 2403.06963 ("The pitfalls of next-token prediction"). Under teacher forcing, later tokens become predictable from the revealed prefix (their "Clever Hans" failure). D1 is a specific instance.
* **Claim line:** "to our knowledge the latent-CoT step-supervision literature does not note that teacher-forced step strings leave result tokens predictable from in-context operands, so they put no pressure on the latent to hold results. Shown formally (D1) and measured (0.880 vs 0.894); an instance of the teacher-forcing Clever Hans failure."
* **External check (pre-stated before any output; $0, local, descriptive).** It runs only if the released SIM-CoT checkpoint (internlm/SIM_COT-GPT2-Coconut checkpoint_28; docs/GSM8K_REPRO.md) contains its step decoder.
  - **Measurement:** on GSM8K-Aug valid, teacher-force each step string through SIM-CoT's step decoder, reading the true latent z_k vs a zeroed or mean latent. Report top-1 by token category: operands, operator, value.
  - **D1 predicts:** value-token top-1 without z_k within 0.05 of top-1 with it, while operand top-1 drops by ≥ 0.20.
  - **Falsifier (for this external instance):** value top-1 drops by ≥ 0.15 without z_k.
  - If the decoder is not in the release, the check is N/A and is not substituted.

**Note 204-2: the external D1 check on SIM-CoT (2026-10-14 19:28 EDT; note 204-1's pre-stated check; Experiments 00d08bc4, script 453f1ebc; boxes/runs_fsq/s204_simcot_d1/eval_simcot_d1.json; internlm SIM_COT-GPT2-Coconut checkpoint_28's own step decoder, expainable_llm; 3070 fp32; Aug valid 500, stages 1–4 primary). MIXED by the letter: supported under MEAN, falsified under ZERO.**
* **Teacher-forced top-1, stages 1–4, TRUE / ZERO / MEAN:**
  - value (n 1,613): 0.939 / 0.447 / 0.915;
  - q-operands: 0.692 / 0.029 / 0.091;
  - r-operands: 0.530 / 0.024 / 0.053;
  - operator: 0.744 / 0.210 / 0.386;
  - format: 0.963 / 0.499 / 0.999;
  - EOS: 0.999 / 0.680 / 0.993.
* **The rule as pre-stated:** value within 0.05 without z_k; operands drop ≥ 0.20; falsifier: value drop ≥ 0.15. The note named "a zeroed or mean latent" without making either one primary.
  - **MEAN** (the per-stage mean latent pair): value drop 0.024, operand drops 0.60 / 0.48. **As D1 predicts.**
  - **ZERO** (an all-zero latent pair): value drop 0.49. **Falsified as written.**
* **Interpretation (stated after the output, not a re-ruling):**
  - ZERO also degrades tokens that need no item information: format 0.963 → 0.499 and EOS 0.999 → 0.680, while MEAN keeps them at 0.99.
  - That pattern fits an off-distribution prefix (the decoder never saw an all-zero latent pair) rather than result tokens that depend on the latent.
  - MEAN is the in-distribution "no item information" condition. Under it, SIM-CoT's step decoder reads results from the in-context operands (0.915 vs 0.939) and needs the latent only for operand and plan identity.
  - Our own D1 measurement used M = 0, which is a natural in-distribution state for DeltaMem (the pass-0 memory). That is unlike SIM-CoT's input-embedding prefix.
* **Stage 5 (merged steps, n 82, descriptive):** value 0.707 / 0.350 / 0.713. MEAN again matches TRUE. *(Correction 19:38, Audit: n 82 is the item count; the stage-5 value-token count is 157.)*
* **Wording:** "on the released SIM-CoT GPT-2 checkpoint, replacing the step latents with their mean leaves value-token accuracy at 0.915 (vs 0.939) while operand accuracy falls to 0.05–0.09", with the ZERO falsification reported beside it.

**Note 204-3 (2026-10-14 19:58 EDT; before any §204 output; measurement definitions, no rule change; Audit's review of the harness 781f678d).**
* **Pointer collisions.**
  - The ptr*_acc candidate sets are deduplicated *first BPE tokens*, so operands that share a first token collapse into one candidate.
  - Gate 3 reports the collision rate: the share of pointer targets whose first token is shared with another candidate.
  - PLAN-ACC for the pointers is reported on all items and on collision-free items. The registered P-F1 reads the all-items value, with collision-free beside it.
* **One equality across arms.**
  - Any reading that compares the factor / value arms with the string arm (P-F1's proxies, P-F9, any VALUE-EXACT vs VALUE-IN-STRING contrast) uses **string equality**: the factor arm's greedy value output is decoded to a string and compared with the gold RHS string, exactly as the string arm's value_in_string does.
  - Token-id equality is reported beside it for the factor arm only.

**Note 204-4 (2026-10-14 20:12 EDT; before any §204 output; a gate-procedure deviation, stated). Gate 9 (RMS invariance of the additive read at γ = 0) cannot run in fp64 on the code path, because deltamem casts to fp32 internally.**
* **Run instead:**
  - (i) The code path in fp32: spread of the RMS additive read across t = 1..4 is 3.4e-7. A_t vs t·A_1 agrees to 3.3e-6.
  - (ii) The fp64 analytic check: rms of t·A_1 is invariant to 4.7e-13.
  - (iii) Controls: the delta read differs across t (0.52). The no-norm raw read is ∝ t (fp64 1.2e-15; code 8.6e-7).
* **Pass criterion, fixed now:** (i) ≤ 1e-5 relative, (ii) ≤ 1e-10, and both controls behave as derived. **All met.**
* **Why this is not the exactness-gate case:** the fp64 rule protects claims that an optimisation computes the same function. Gate 9 checks a mathematical property of an existing read. The fp64 analytic check carries the property, and the fp32 code check shows the implementation matches it at fp32 rounding.

**Note 204-5 (2026-10-14 20:24 EDT; post-freeze, before any §204 output, W not landed; docs/THEORY_LOTUS_CONTRAST_2026-10-14.md, Opus subagent, Theory-reviewed: capacity margin 24x items / 2-12x bits, LOTUS teacherless per its v2 eqs. 1-3). LOTUS-SEP: is LOTUS's per-loop use (2606.31779) explained by teacherless supervision (ii) or by channel width (i)?**
* **Inputs:** read from §204's registered fields on F-P vs its comparator (W, or A on the A base), on paired test items.
  - deep = m ≥ 3 (n 879); "ratio" = the raw K′1/K′10 on deep items;
  - "floor" = the M_0 reading;
  - VALUE-SERIAL = P-F3's letter (VALUE-EXACT from M_t ≥ floor + 0.10, and VALUE-LEAK ≤ floor + 0.05, on ℓ ≥ 2 R-steps at t = 2–3).
* **One added descriptive eval field, $0:** VALUE-EXACT and PLAN-ACC at pass 1 on level-1 steps, by m (≤ 2 vs ≥ 4).
* **Readings:**
  - **(ii)-SUFFICIENT:** ratio(F-P) ≤ ratio(comparator) − 0.20, and VALUE-SERIAL.
  - **DECODER-SHORTCUT:** VALUE-SERIAL, but ratio(F-P) > ratio(comparator) − 0.10. The memory carries results that the answer path does not use, which points to (i-b) read geometry, not width.
  - **WIDTH-CANDIDATE:** all three of:
    - VALUE-EXACT from M_t on ℓ ≥ 2 R-steps ≤ floor + 0.05;
    - ratio(F-P) > ratio(comparator) − 0.10;
    - INTERFERENCE: pass-1 VALUE-EXACT on level-1 steps lower by ≥ 0.10 on m ≥ 4 than on m ≤ 2, **and** that drop exceeds the same drop in PLAN-ACC by ≥ 0.05 (the difficulty control).
  - **CARRY-FAILS:** as WIDTH-CANDIDATE without INTERFERENCE. Results are not carried, but not by interference (A-OP or learnability).
  - **INCONCLUSIVE:** otherwise, e.g. a delta in (−0.20, −0.10].
* **Noise:** the deep ratio's SE is ≈ 0.08 per cell (0.03–0.12), so a paired difference has SE ≈ 0.11, and −0.20 ≈ 1.8 SE. The per-item rows (§204 gate) give the bootstrap, reported beside.
* **Pre-stated P (A base / W base):**
  - (ii)-SUFFICIENT 0.25 / 0.35;
  - DECODER-SHORTCUT 0.25 / 0.25;
  - WIDTH-CANDIDATE 0.05 / 0.05;
  - CARRY-FAILS 0.15 / 0.10;
  - INCONCLUSIVE 0.30 / 0.25.
* **Consequence:** only WIDTH-CANDIDATE motivates a width cell. DECODER-SHORTCUT motivates a read-geometry change (the answer reading memory at more layers) as its own derivation.
* Descriptive, one seed. It changes no §204 rule.

## 205. IIT-SERIAL: a whole-state interchange loss for seed stability (USER APPROVED 2026-10-15 ~01:4x, "Approve", typed in Audit's session and relayed verbatim; FULL / default design; cap $18; pre-registered 2026-10-15 01:49 EDT, before any §205 training run)

**Registered text:**
* docs/THEORY_IITSERIAL_DRAFT_2026-10-14.md **at 13d7bb87** is the registered text for every definition below: the loss §2, derivation §3, Goodhart §4, gradient flow §5, C1 §6, design / labels / predictions §7, and the addenda (G-ALIGN by n, motivation, measured cost / OC / censoring, slow-host bound).
* That file is now frozen. Changes go here as dated amendments.
* Derivation by Opus subagent, reviewed by Theory and Audit.
* Code: --iit (27d05cef / 62343096), Audit-reviewed. G-TIME and G-MEM done (≈ $0.12).

**Why (data, POST-HOC):**
* 203-4 CONTRAST-SURVIVES: converged seeds follow a whole-state swap (clean hybrid ≥ 0.80); failed seeds ignore it (≤ 0.18).
* 203-8: failed seeds follow a swapped input instead (0.90–0.99), Huginn-like recomputation.
* 203-7: seed selection by loss features does not work.
* The loss trains state USE, not presence, coordinate-free. It is PROVED not to be meetable by accuracy alone (y_hyb ≠ y on every used pair), and a δ-contractive model pays a floor.

**Cells (RTX 3090, 48k):**
* `s205_iit_s1` / `s2` / `s3` = s185_rms_s{seed}'s args exactly + `--iit 1.0,0.5,16` (w_IIT 1, w_SIIT 0.5, B_I 16; swap after τ = 1; weight ∝ γ(step), so bitwise to step 2000) + `--keep_ckpt_steps 4000,8000,12000,16000`. ckpt_model_8000.pt is kept (retention default).
* **Pairing:** log records 100–2000 bitwise equal to s185_rms_s{seed} on loss / answer_ce / aux_ce, on that control's driver (s1 / s2 570.172.08, s3 595.84). Otherwise UNPAIRED.
* Seeds run in parallel on separate hosts (one filler at a time).
* **Pre-launch gates passed:** G-ALIGN (203-3), G-TIME, G-MEM. G-HYB, G-GRAD and G-PLAIN are per the code review.

**Readings** (draft §7; theory/score_s205.py, fixture-checked before landing):
* **Per seed:**
  - **MET** = iit_eval clean-ccc hybrid ≥ 0.8 at τ = 1;
  - **ENTERED** = entry(0.5) ≤ 24k and final 1k bin < 0.1;
  - labels ENTERED-AND-MET / MET-NOT-ENTERED / ENTERED-NOT-MET / NEITHER;
  - **HARMFUL:** s1 or s2 never enters;
  - **ONE-PASS-COMPUTE:** g1 > 0.20 or g2 > 0.21;
  - **CLEAN-CONTRACTIVE:** MET with acc_from_donor > 0.2 or delta_cos > 0.65.
* **Arm:**
  - **SUPPORTED** = 3 / 3 ENTERED-AND-MET, none HARMFUL / ONE-PASS-COMPUTE / CLEAN-CONTRACTIVE;
  - **FAILED** = any HARMFUL, any MET-NOT-ENTERED, or 0 / 3 MET;
  - else MIXED.
* **Account falsifier:** MET-NOT-ENTERED in any seed.
* **Predictions** P-I1–P-I7 as in the draft. **Descriptive:** the 8k direction tests (203-4 swap-follow, 203-6 input swap) on ckpt_model_8000.pt, and the deep-n push on the good class (draft addendum).

**OC block (rule a):**
* MET is trained directly, so ENTERED is the informative label.
* P(3 / 3 entered) ≈ 0.27–0.30 with no effect on entry vs ≈ 0.86 with an effect (p 0.95), each × P(MET 3 / 3) ≈ 0.6. **The likelihood ratio is about 3, so this is a pilot; a positive needs a second-stage panel** (the user's call).
* s3 is the informative seed: P(s3 enters | no effect) ≈ 0.6.

**Censoring (rule b):**
* A seed that never reaches entry(0.5) by 48k, dies or is aborted is NOT ENTERED: a failure, not missing.
* The event-only mean entry step is reported beside it.

**Cost:** measured 1.464 s/step after turn-on, about 18.8 h per seed. That is about $14 typical for 3 seeds and **≤ $18 (slow-host bound; the approved cap)**, with a running guard at $18. Realised $ replaces the projection.

## 207. GSM-SWAP: is GSM8K's one-pass dominance the failed nested seeds' "recompute from the input" mode? (descriptive, $0 eval-only on kept models; Audit's lead; pre-stated 2026-10-15 09:57 EDT, before any output)

**Why:**
* On nested, failed seeds ignore a swapped state and follow a swapped input (203-4 / 203-8), while converged seeds carry the state.
* Every GSM8K latent model so far is one-pass-dominated: K′1/K′10 0.74–0.95, THINK-NECESSARY fails.
* Is that the same input-recomputing mode? GSM8K problems have no shared tree shape, so no exact hybrid exists. The test uses own / donor answers and memory-free floors instead.

**Models:** final model.pt of A gsm_lat_aug_s1, B gsm_lat_augrs_s1, W gsm_lat_warm_s1, F-P gsm_lat_factor_s1, J1 gsm_lat_jcotl1_s1, and J0 gsm_lat_jcot_s1 when it lands.
* One local card (3070), bf16, eval_bs 64 (the original eval bs); card / dtype / bs recorded.

**Items:** GSM8K test.
* Recipients x_r = items the model answers correctly clean at K′ = 10.
* Each gets a donor x_d drawn from the same model's clean-correct items (rng 20701), with y_d ≠ y_r (both numeric answers).
* Readable if ≥ 100 recipients. Reported overall and for m ≤ 2 vs m ≥ 3.

**Arms (K = 10):**
* **STATE-SWAP(t), t ∈ {1, 2}:** passes 1..t on x_d, then passes t+1..K and the decoder on x_r. Reported: P(answer = y_r) (OWN-KEPT) and P(answer = y_d).
* **ZERO-STATE:** K′ = 0 on x_r (memory-free), the floor for OWN-KEPT.
* **INPUT-SWAP(k), k ∈ {1, 2}:** passes 1..k on x_r, then passes k+1..K and the decoder on x_d. Reported: P(answer = y_d) (INPUT-FOLLOW) and P(answer = y_r) (CARRIED).
* **INPUT-SWAP-THINK** (descriptive): as INPUT-SWAP, but the decoder keeps x_r's text.

**Readings:**
* **RECOMPUTES-FROM-INPUT** if both hold, on readable models:
  - OWN-KEPT(2) ≥ 0.8 × OWN-KEPT clean (= 1 on clean items, so ≥ 0.8): the swapped state barely moves the answer;
  - INPUT-FOLLOW(1) ≥ 0.8.
* **CARRIES-STATE** if OWN-KEPT(2) ≤ 0.5 and CARRIED(1) ≥ 0.3.
* Otherwise MIXED.
* **Descriptive:**
  - ZERO-STATE vs STATE-SWAP: a misleading memory vs an absent one;
  - J1 / J0 vs W, since §206's J1 is less one-pass-dominated (K′1/K′10 0.64);
  - m ≥ 3 vs m ≤ 2.

**Prediction (central, CONJECTURE):** RECOMPUTES-FROM-INPUT for A / B / W / F-P (OWN-KEPT(2) about 0.85, INPUT-FOLLOW about 0.85), and MIXED for J1.

**Gates:**
* x_d = x_r reproduces the clean answers bitwise at the same bs / card.
* The plain path is bitwise.
* A new script; no boxes/*.py edits.

**Note 207-1 (2026-10-15 09:58 EDT; before any §207 output; interpretation guard, Audit).**
* **CARRIES-STATE means "the answer lives in the memory"** (serial use OR pass-1 precompute), not "serial use".
  - §204 showed a pass-1 precompute: VALUE-LEAK ≈ 0.9, PROBE-LEAK ≥ 0.92.
  - A model that writes its whole answer at pass 1 follows a donor state at t = 2 and keeps its own answer under an input swap from k = 1.
* **Disambiguation (pre-stated):**
  - **SERIAL-CARRY** if CARRIED(2) − CARRIED(1) ≥ 0.10. More passes on the own input carry more.
  - **PASS1-CARRY** if |CARRIED(2) − CARRIED(1)| ≤ 0.05. The answer is already in the memory after pass 1.
  - Otherwise CARRY-AMBIGUOUS.
  - The same contrast is reported for OWN-KEPT under STATE-SWAP: OWN-KEPT(1) vs (2), so a serial user loses more when swapped later.
* **K′1 / K′10** is reported beside it.
* **No §207 label is read as the nested "converged" signature without SERIAL-CARRY.**

**§207 result, 5 of 6 models (2026-10-15 10:05 EDT; Experiments 7fd4fa69, scratch/gsm_swap.py, 3070 bf16 bs 64; G-PLAIN bitwise on all 5; J0 pending). Every GSM8K latent model recomputes from the input: a swapped input takes over and a carried answer never survives. The nested failed-seed mode, on GSM8K.**
* **Results** on clean-correct recipients (n 180–209):

  | model | ZERO-STATE own | STATE-SWAP(2) own (OWN-KEPT) | INPUT-SWAP(1) donor (INPUT-FOLLOW) | INPUT-SWAP(1) own (CARRIED) | reading |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | A | 0.309 | 0.866 | 0.907 | 0.005 | RECOMPUTES-FROM-INPUT |
  | B | 0.196 | 0.799 | 0.876 | 0.000 | MIXED by the literal 0.8 (see below) |
  | W | 0.510 | 0.880 | 0.917 | 0.000 | RECOMPUTES-FROM-INPUT |
  | F-P | 0.342 | 0.826 | 0.870 | 0.000 | RECOMPUTES-FROM-INPUT |
  | J1 | 0.289 | 0.867 | 0.917 | 0.000 | RECOMPUTES-FROM-INPUT |

  - INPUT-SWAP(2) donor: 0.81–0.85.
  - STATE-SWAP(2) own: similar at m ≤ 2 and m ≥ 3.
* **B's borderline, stated:** the registered text reads "OWN-KEPT(2) ≥ 0.8 × OWN-KEPT clean (= 1 on clean items, so ≥ 0.8)".
  - On the arm-batch layout B's clean (IDENTITY) is 0.995, a bf16 layout flip of 1 item in 209. The ratio form would then be ≥ 0.796, which B's 0.799 meets.
  - Choosing the ratio after seeing the output would be post hoc, so **B is MIXED by the literal threshold, and the ratio reading is reported beside it.** The difference is one item.
* **Note 207-1:** CARRIED is 0.000–0.005 at k = 1, so no model carries its answer in memory at all. CARRIES-STATE, SERIAL-CARRY and PASS1-CARRY all do not apply.
* **Prediction:** central RECOMPUTES for A / B / W / F-P holds for A / W / F-P (B borderline). **"J1 MIXED" is FALSIFIED: J1 recomputes too,** despite its lower K′1 / K′10 (0.64).
* **Descriptive:**
  - **A misleading memory is far better than none.** OWN-KEPT under a swapped state is 0.80–0.88, against 0.20–0.51 with ZERO-STATE.
  - So the models need a memory to be present, an in-distribution scaffold, but ignore its item-specific content and recompute the answer from the re-read question.
  - INPUT-SWAP-THINK (the decoder keeps x_r) own is 0.13–0.45: when only the think passes see the donor question, the answer degrades, so the think passes matter as computation on the current input, not as a carried state.
* **Reading:**
  - GSM8K's one-pass dominance is the nested failed seeds' "recompute from the input" mode (203-4 / 203-8; Huginn 2609.01924), in every GSM8K latent recipe tried (raw, resampled, warm-started, factored, joint-CoT plus coupling).
  - On GSM8K the latent memory is a scaffold, not a carrier. This is the most direct account yet of why the latent arm sits below text.
  - It points at an interchange-type objective for GSM8K (the IIT-SERIAL logic) as the matching lever. That would be its own derivation, as GSM8K lacks an exact hybrid target.
* *(Added 10:05; Audit's independent reproduction from the five eval_gswap.json files.)*
  - **B: "a 0.001 miss, descriptively the same pattern".** The rule form is not changed post hoc.
  - **Presence ≠ use again:** the memory carries a generic "has thought" signal the decoder depends on (zero-state 0.20–0.51 vs donor-state 0.80–0.88), but no item-specific content it uses. Cf. §203 G-use and note 204-2's ZERO vs MEAN.
  - **This reconciles §204:** VALUE-LEAK shows the values are DECODABLE from M_1 by the aux decoder, while §207 shows the answer decoder does not USE them; it recomputes from the question.

## 208. QUESTION-ONCE + ANSWER-BOTTLENECK + NOPASS: can memory-only passes compute GSM8K? (USER APPROVED 2026-10-15, "Approve both", typed in Audit's session and relayed verbatim; user approval typed ~11:0x–11:15 EDT (Audit's time error corrected; it was first relayed as "~12:0x"); one cell; cap $3.20; pre-registered 2026-10-15 11:16 EDT, before any §208 code or run)

**Registered text:**
* docs/THEORY_QONCE_DRAFT_2026-10-15.md **at 1c2dc4d3** (including §16, the aux-prompt choice) is the registered text for every definition below.
* For the answer-bottleneck decoder's definitions and swap labels it uses docs/THEORY_ANSBOTTLE_DRAFT_2026-10-15.md at b890ae81, as the QO draft references it.
* Both files are now frozen. Changes go here as dated amendments.
* Derivations by Opus subagent, reviewed by Theory and Audit. Literature f4c7c197: new for latent reasoning.

**Why (data, POST-HOC):**
* §207: every GSM8K latent model recomputes from the re-presented question; the memory is a scaffold, not a carrier.
* §204 / §206: per-pass targets and a pre-answer coupling are met by pass-1 precompute or by the decoder, not by the memory.
* Internal precedent: §165 FIXED-CHUNK (question once, a problem-free decoder, final-answer-only training) failed. §175 showed that per-pass supervision makes the passes used. Question-once with the step aux has never run.

**Cell:** `gsm_lat_ansbn_qonce_nopass_s1` = §200 A's flags exactly + `--ans_bottleneck --question_once --aux_nopass` (no RMS).
* Think pass 1 reads [EOT, question]. Passes 2–10 read the fixed 17-token filler (EOT + FILLER-N's string).
* The answer decoder reads [EOT, "###"] + the memory only.
* The aux prompt is [EOT, " Step", " :"].
* RTX 3090, seed 1, 24k. Final checkpoint for every reading; the test is never used for selection.

**Decisive reading, ITER-GAIN (comparator-free; PROVED from the code that passes 2–10 are item-identical functions except through the memory):**
* ACC − max(MEAN-ITER(1), K′1) ≥ T = 0.028 pooled, **and** the deep version (m ≥ 3) ≥ T_D = 0.034.
* K′1-RESCALED is reported only (it is wrong under QO; §16).

**Labels (draft §5 / §7):**
* **QO-SERIAL** (the C1 success) = ITER-GAIN ∧ SERIAL-PROFILE (an onset growing with m) ∧ (TRANSPLANT-SERIAL ∨ INT-PROGRESS).
* **TWO-STAGE / DENOISE:** ITER-GAIN with a flat onset. Multi-pass use, not serial.
* **PASS1-PRECOMPUTE:** no ITER-GAIN; capped at about 0.13.
* **QO-CAPACITY-BOUND** vs **QO-COMPUTE-FAIL:** by the literal-recall probes and the accuracy-vs-literal-count slope.
* ACC vs A (LIFTS / MATCHES / HURTS) is reported. It is two changes against A, so attribution between AB and QO rests on the probes.
* The clock readout (pairs 2v3, 3v4, 5v6) is descriptive.

**OC block (rule a; one seed):**
* P(QO-SERIAL | no effect) ≈ 0.005–0.01; P(QO-SERIAL | effect) ≈ 0.2–0.4.
* ITER-GAIN alone: P(| no effect) ≈ 0.02 by sampling (≈ 0.2 if "no effect" means "no serial use", since TWO-STAGE also passes).
* **A positive is strong evidence; a null is weak; a rate claim needs ≥ 3 seeds.**

**Censoring (rule b; draft §9):**
* A run ending before 24k, dying or aborted: every reading fails.
* A MEAN-ITER replay failing its identity gate: ITER-GAIN not credited.
* An unreadable ONSET: SERIAL-PROFILE not met.
* Unreadable transplant and probes: QO-SERIAL fails.
* answer_ce never ≤ 0.92 per token: NO-ENTRY, a failure.
* Event-only values are reported beside each.

**Prior (CONJECTURE):** ACC central 0.075 (HURTS about 0.7); P(ITER-GAIN) about 0.36; P(QO-SERIAL) about 0.16; PASS1 about 0.42. The main risk is the lossy-copy basin: per-literal fidelity ρ below about 0.72.

**Gates (draft §12 + §16):**
* the plain path bitwise (G1, including that `--aux_nopass` alone reproduces §204's NOPASS path bitwise, and the AB / QO helpers in FactorMem as well as ProsMem);
* per-term gradflow;
* mem_check;
* an assert that the answer decoder's input ids contain no question token;
* the MEAN-ITER identity gate;
* G-TIME (replaces the cost projection);
* Audit's diff review;
* a running guard at $3.20.

**Cost:** $2.0 central / $3.0 high (passes 2–10 skip the question, so it is cheaper per item than A). Approved cap $3.20. Realised $ replaces the projection.

**Note 208-1 (2026-10-15 11:40 EDT; before any §208 output; a procedure change, Audit's call on the timing).** The MEAN-ITER replay identity gate (G6), and the rest of the eval-only §5 script (MEAN-ITER(k), ONSET, transplant, LIT-RECALL / INT-PROGRESS / ANS-LIN, the clock readout), may be built while the cell trains, instead of before launch.
* These are eval-only analyses of the final model.pt; nothing has to be recorded during training.
* **G6 must pass on the smoke QO model before the cell lands,** and on the final model before any ITER-GAIN read.
* The registered censoring already covers a failure: a MEAN-ITER replay failing its identity gate means ITER-GAIN is not credited.
* The training-path gates (G1–G5, the no-question-token assert, G-TIME) stay before launch.

**Note 208-2 (2026-10-15 12:40 EDT; before any §208 output; the scorer's operational definitions, no rule change).** theory/score_s208.py, fixture-checked on seven synthetic panels: QO-SERIAL, TWO-STAGE, PASS1-PRECOMPUTE, G6 failing, a run dying at 15k, NO-ENTRY, pending.
* **Readings use the local fp32 eval** (eval_qonce.json): ACC = clean_fp32, K′ and MEAN-ITER from kprime_fp32 / mean_iter. That keeps the decisive comparison within one dtype. The on-host bf16 eval.json supplies ACC vs A and the reported K′1-RESCALED.
* **MEAN-ITER's item mean is over all 1,319 test items** (batch-independent) rather than "the batch mean" of the draft. This is Experiments' choice, adopted before output. The item's own 1/1319 share is negligible.
* **SERIAL-PROFILE, operationally:** ONSET is non-decreasing over the resolvable strata (1, 2, 3, 4, 5+), and min ONSET over strata {4, 5+} ≥ max ONSET over strata {1, 2} + 2. ONESHOT-PROFILE = one ONSET across every resolvable stratum. Fewer than 3 resolvable strata is UNREADABLE.
* **The chance level for MEMORY-CARRIES / MEMORY-FAILS = K′0 accuracy (fp32),** the zero-memory constant answer and the measured proxy for P_test(y = c).
* **QO-CAPACITY-BOUND's FIDELITY branch is read without the difficulty control** (A's aux-slot operand drop is not in eval_qonce), and this is stated beside it. RETENTION needs no control.
* **G6 failing gives "ITER-GAIN NOT CREDITED" and no route label.** The route labels require a credited ITER-GAIN reading.

**§208 result (2026-10-15 15:24 EDT; gsm_lat_ansbn_qonce_nopass_s1, b301, 3090 595.91.07, 24k, realised about $0.88 of $3.20; local fp32 eval_qonce.json with G6 passing on the final model; theory/score_s208.py). PASS1-PRECOMPUTE: with the question shown only to pass 1 and a memory-only decoder, one forward pass computes the answer and later passes add nothing. Accuracy MATCHES A.**
* **ITER-GAIN fails:** ACC 0.138 vs max(MEAN-ITER(1) 0.142, K′1 0.143), so −0.005 pooled and −0.007 on m ≥ 3.
  - K′ 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 10 / 16 = 0.014 / 0.143 / 0.140 / 0.143 / 0.138 / 0.130.
  - K′0 is the constant answer " 30", so the bottleneck holds and the answer crosses the memory.
* **ONSET = 1 in every stratum** (m 1, 2, 3, 4, 5+): ONESHOT-PROFILE.
* **PROGRESS-TRANSPLANT:** P_hyb 0.000 in every cell (C_t2 n 449, S_t2 n 130). P_own 0.97–1.00: the answer follows the recipient's pass-1 content and ignores the donor's passes 2..t. TRANSPLANT-SERIAL is not met.
* **INT-PROGRESS: not met.** The ℓ ≥ 2 values from M_{ℓ+1} and from M_1 are both at chance (0.096 vs the M_0 floor 0.109).
* **Capacity: QO-CAPACITY-BOUND does not fire.**
  - R_QO = 0.42 = R_A (0.42): no extra literal-count penalty.
  - LIT-RECALL(1) 0.339 vs floors ≤ 0.046; LIT-RECALL(10) 0.316, so no RETENTION loss.
  - The FIDELITY drop (0.176) is within A's 0.142 + 0.10.
  - QO-COMPUTE-FAIL does not fire either (ACC > A − T).
* **ACC vs A: MATCHES** (−0.011). STABLE-12 and STABLE-16 hold. Entry (answer_ce ≤ 0.92) at 8.2k.
* **Descriptive:**
  - ANS-LIN: the answer's first token is linearly decodable from the final read at 0.117 (decoder 0.196, ratio 0.60).
  - Clock pairs 2v3 / 3v4 / 5v6: 0.755 / 0.700 / 0.650.
* **Predictions:** the prior's modal label (PASS1, about 0.42) held. The prior "ACC HURTS (about 0.7), central 0.075" missed: ACC matched A.
* **Reading:**
  - **At this budget the GSM8K latent arm's whole accuracy is a single forward pass.** With the question visible only to pass 1 and a decoder that sees nothing but the memory, pass 1 computes the answer (about 0.14) and writes it; passes 2–10 neither add to nor use it.
  - Together with §207 (every earlier recipe recomputes from the re-read question), this is the clearest statement of the GSM8K state: **no recipe tried has learned memory-mediated multi-pass computation on GSM8K at about 4 epochs. The about 0.14 is GPT-2-small's one-pass accuracy at this budget.**
  - §209 (CODI at the same budget) decides whether a published latent design does better at this budget (architecture) or not (budget).
  - The QO draft's named next lever was copy fidelity. It is NOT indicated: the copy was fine and capacity did not bind. The binding fact is that one pass suffices for what the model learned. Any multi-pass gain needs a training signal that one pass cannot meet.

## 209. CODI-AT-OUR-BUDGET: is GSM8K's latent shortfall architecture or budget? (USER APPROVED 2026-10-15 ~11:37 EDT, "approve reccomendation", typed in Audit's session and relayed verbatim; one cell; cap $4; pre-registered 2026-10-15 11:39 EDT, before any §209 code or run)

**Question:**
* All in-house GSM8K latent arms sit at about 0.14–0.15 after about 4 epochs of GSM8K-Aug (A 0.147, B 0.160, W 0.146, F-P 0.139, J0 0.144, J1 0.138). Text CoT C sits at 0.321 at the same budget.
* Published latent methods reach 0.42–0.44, but at 20–40 epochs (note 202-2).
* Our eval port scores the released CODI checkpoint (zen-E/CODI-gpt2) at 42.5 vs 43.7 published (docs/GSM8K_REPRO.md), so the evaluation is not the gap.
* **Is the remaining gap our DeltaMem architecture, or the budget?**

**Design (one change against the published method: the budget):**
* **Cell `gsm_codi_4ep_s1`:** CODI's GPT-2 small design trained in our pipeline on our data (GSM8K-Aug, 385k; the same test and eval as §200), at **4.0 epochs** (≈ 1.54M examples, as §200's 24k × 64).
* **Architecture:**
  - 6 continuous latents generated autoregressively, the last-layer state fed back through CODI's projection (MLP + LN);
  - LoRA r 128 / α 32 at lr 3e-3;
  - joint teacher CE plus the per-layer teacher-std-normalised L1 at the token before the answer (the ":" of "The answer is:"), with sg on the teacher;
  - the teacher's CoT drops its last step;
  - γ (teacher-CE weight) = 2: CODI's best at its shortest reported budget (Table A5; Literature bc8be322). All other weights are CODI's GPT-2 values.
* RTX 3090, seed 1, final checkpoint; the test is never used for selection.
* **Evaluation:** CODI's own test recipe through our existing port (theory/codi_probe.py: question + `<bot>`, 6 latents, `<eot>`, greedy, the answer after "The answer is:") on the 1,319 test items.

**Why 4 epochs is informative (DERIVED, assumptions stated):**
* At 4 epochs our text CoT C reaches 0.321, about 0.75 of the long-budget GPT-2 CoT-SFT level (0.427–0.441).
* CODI's own anchors are 0.384 at 20 epochs and 0.437 at 40 (γ 1), with γ 2 faster but lower at the end (0.416 / 0.419).
* **A1 (assumption):** if the latent method's budget curve is no slower than text's, CODI at 4 epochs ≈ 0.75 × 0.42 ≈ 0.31. If it is much slower (the latents needing many epochs to become useful), CODI at 4 epochs falls toward our latent level.
* The 4-epoch point therefore separates "a latent method works at this budget and ours doesn't" (architecture-bound) from "latent methods need more budget" (budget-bound). Both readings name a different next spend (§209's step 2, a separate decision).

**Decision rule** (on the in-house equal-budget scale; r = (CODI4 − A) / (C − A), with A 0.147 and C 0.321, gap 0.174):
* **ARCHITECTURE-BOUND:** CODI4 ≥ 0.251 (r ≥ 0.6). A published latent design closes most of the latent / text gap at our budget, so our DeltaMem design is the GSM8K bottleneck.
* **BUDGET-BOUND:** CODI4 ≤ 0.175 (≤ A + T, T = 0.028). CODI is no better than ours at this budget, so budget is the lever.
* **MIXED:** otherwise.
* Beside it: CODI4 − C (vs text), the valid curve (is it still rising at 4 epochs?), and CODI4's K-latent ablation (0 vs 6 latents), descriptive.

**OC block (rule a; one seed):**
* The test SE is about 0.012. The seed SD on GSM8K is unknown; take 0.01–0.02, so a combined SD of about 0.016–0.023.
* P(ARCH-BOUND | true CODI4 0.20) ≈ 0.001–0.013; P(ARCH-BOUND | true 0.30) ≈ 0.983–0.999.
* P(BUDGET-BOUND | true 0.15) ≈ 0.86–0.94; P(BUDGET-BOUND | true 0.22) ≈ 0.003–0.025 (normal approximation, computed).
* **Misreads need a true value within about 1 SD of a boundary.** That zone is reported as such.

**Censoring (rule b):**
* A run that dies before 4 epochs gives NO reading (UNREAD, not a default label). Logs are kept; a re-run happens only under a new name and with approval.
* A valid curve missing a record is reported as missing.

**Gates (before launch):**
* (G1) The eval port scores the released zen-E/CODI-gpt2 at 42.5, bitwise to §13's probe on the same card / bs.
* (G2) Per-term gradflow: the student CE, the teacher CE and the L1 each reach LoRA; sg holds on the teacher states.
* (G3) LoRA's trainable-parameter count and target modules match CODI's released config.
* (G4) A smoke at about 200 steps: the loss falls and the latents are generated autoregressively.
* (G5) mem_check.
* (G6) G-TIME (replaces the cost projection).
* Audit's diff review; a running guard at $4.

**Cost:** CODI GPT-2 at 40 epochs ≈ 36 A100-h, so about 3.6 A100-h for 4 epochs, ≈ 6–8 h on a 3090, ≈ $1.6–2.2 at $0.25–0.28 / h, plus hosts. **Cap $4.** Realised $ replaces the projection.

**Next (not registered here):** budget scaling (~20 epochs) of whichever design wins, as a separate decision with its own cost.

**Note 209-1 (2026-10-15 11:40 EDT; before any §209 code or run; design pins, Audit's review).**
* **Label:** the cell is "CODI recipe, γ 2 (the 4-epoch prior), not CODI's published γ 1".
* **Hyperparameters follow CODI's paper / released config except the budget (the one registered change):**
  - LoRA r 128 / α 32 on CODI's target modules;
  - AdamW at lr 3e-3, cosine with 3% warm-up;
  - **batch size 128 (CODI's), not our 64**;
  - 6 latents plus the projection (MLP + LN);
  - the teacher's last step dropped;
  - weights per CODI's GPT-2 config, with γ = 2 as labelled.
